package_info.package_manager: proprietary (commercial software, not public package manager)
package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 through 2020.2.1 (as per public reporting, but not specified in this report)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package is considered malicious because attackers injected a backdoor into the build process, resulting in digitally signed, production-distributed software containing attacker-controlled code. This allowed widespread compromise of downstream users and organizations.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if it is running in the expected process, then periodically beacons to a hardcoded command-and-control (C2) domain, receives commands, and executes them, enabling remote attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This behavior is suspicious because legitimate software should not contain hidden code that communicates with external attacker-controlled domains or executes remote commands.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not include hidden backdoors or C2 communication logic, especially in digitally signed, production releases.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may beacon to central servers, but this is always documented, user-controlled, and not hidden in production code.
key_indicators: Hidden network beaconing to external domains
Code injected during build, not present in source

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to build infrastructure (via credential compromise, insider, or misconfiguration).
Malicious code is injected into the Orion software during the build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in digitally signed production releases.

attack_chain.action: Compromised Orion software is distributed to customers via normal update channels.
At runtime, the malicious code beacons to attacker-controlled domains and receives commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote attacker control of victim environments.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network connections from Orion software to external, non-SolarWinds domains
Periodic beaconing behavior from business layer host processes
Execution of commands received from remote servers
file_indicators: Presence of code not present in official source repositories
Digitally signed binaries with unexpected code sections
network_indicators: Connections to known SolarWinds C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com, other attacker infrastructure)
Unusual DNS queries or HTTP/S requests from Orion servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from SolarWinds Orion servers, especially to domains not associated with SolarWinds. Analyze Orion DLLs for code sections not present in official releases. Use EDR or AV tools to detect beaconing or command execution behavior. Validate digital signatures and compare file hashes against known-good versions. Monitor build infrastructure for unauthorized changes to build artifacts.
